recommendedTextbook.title: Basic Civic Education for Junior Secondary Schools 1
recommendedTextbook.author: M.O. Adebayo, S.A. Falade, E.O. Ajibola

topics.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Civic Education in Nigeria
subtopics: Definition of Civic Education as the study of citizenship rights and duties
Historical origins and need for civic training in Nigerian schools
Objectives: fostering patriotism, national unity, democratic culture, and civic responsibility
objectives: Define Civic Education and state four primary objectives of teaching it in Nigerian schools
Explain how civic awareness reduces ethnic prejudice and promotes national cohesion

topics.topic: National Values I: Honesty and Integrity in Daily Conduct
subtopics: Meaning of personal and civic values
Attributes of honesty (truthfulness, transparency, refusing examination malpractice)
Benefits of honesty to the individual, school, and Nigerian society
Consequences of dishonesty (distrust, criminal sanctions, national reputational damage)
objectives: Explain why honesty is the foundation of character and national development
Analyze real-life school scenarios where moral integrity must be upheld

topics.topic: National Values II: Cooperation and Teamwork for Nation Building
subtopics: Meaning and attributes of cooperation
Factors that promote cooperation: mutual trust, shared goals, justice, open communication
Benefits of community self-help projects in Nigerian towns and villages
objectives: List four benefits of cooperation in school sports teams and community sanitation
Participate collaboratively in a classroom clean-up exercise

topics.topic: National Values III: Self-Reliance and Entrepreneurship
subtopics: Meaning of self-reliance (ability to support oneself through skills and enterprise)
Attributes of self-reliant individuals: hard work, creativity, financial discipline
Youth vocational skills acquisition in Nigeria (tailoring, computer coding, carpentry, catering)
objectives: Identify benefits of self-reliance in reducing graduate unemployment in Nigeria
Formulate a plan to acquire a practical vocational skill during holiday periods

topics.topic: Nigerian National Symbols: Significance, Design and Respect
subtopics: The National Flag: designed by Pa Taiwo Akinkunmi in 1959 (Green: agriculture, White: peace)
The Coat of Arms: Black shield (fertile soil), White 'Y' (River Niger and Benue confluence), Eagles (strength), Horses (dignity)
The National Anthem, National Pledge, and the National Currency (Naira ₦)
objectives: Draw and color the Nigerian National Flag with correct proportions and explain its colors
Recite the Nigerian National Anthem and Pledge with proper posture and patriotic reverence
Identify elements of the Coat of Arms and explain their symbolic meanings

topics.topic: Citizenship: Meaning, Types and Qualifications under Nigerian Law
subtopics: Definition of a citizen as a legal member of a sovereign state
Types of citizenship in Nigeria: by birth, by registration, by naturalization
Grounds for deprivation or loss of citizenship
objectives: Differentiate citizenship by birth from citizenship by naturalization under the 1999 Constitution
Enumerate conditions required for a foreigner to acquire Nigerian citizenship

subtopics: Evaluation on civic concepts, national values, national symbols, and citizenship types
Remedial civic values workshop
objectives: Assess pupil comprehension against national civic standards

topics.topic: Rights and Duties of Nigerian Citizens under the 1999 Constitution
subtopics: Fundamental Human Rights (Right to Life, Dignity of Human Person, Personal Liberty, Fair Hearing)
Duties and obligations: obeying statutory laws, paying taxes, defending the nation, voting during elections
Differences between rights (legal entitlements) and duties (civic responsibilities)
objectives: List 6 fundamental human rights enshrined in Chapter IV of the 1999 Nigerian Constitution
State four civic duties required of citizens to sustain public infrastructure

topics.topic: The Nigerian Constitution: Meaning, History & Supremacy
subtopics: Definition of a constitution as the supreme body of governing laws of a country
Historical overview of Nigerian constitutions: Clifford (1922), Richards (1946), Macpherson (1951), Lyttelton (1954), 1999 Constitution
Meaning of constitutional supremacy: any law inconsistent with the constitution is null and void
objectives: Explain the supremacy of the constitution over all military decrees and state edicts
Distinguish between written and unwritten constitutions

topics.topic: Road Safety & Traffic Regulations: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
subtopics: Establishment, statutory mandate, and activities of the FRSC in Nigeria
Road signs: regulatory signs (stop, speed limit), warning signs (pedestrian crossing, sharp bend)
Pedestrian safety rules: using zebra crossings, pedestrian pedestrian bridges, walking facing oncoming traffic
objectives: Identify 10 common Nigerian road traffic signs and explain their meanings
State causes of highway accidents (over-speeding, drunk driving, tire blowouts) and safety precautions

topics.topic: Environmental Sanitation and Community Health Obligations
subtopics: Civic obligations to maintain clean, hygienic residential and public environments
Waste disposal protocols and hazards of indiscriminate refuse dumping in drainage canals
Participation in monthly statutory environmental sanitation exercises
objectives: Explain how clogged gutters cause flooding in urban centers like Lagos and Port Harcourt
Formulate a class waste-sorting initiative to encourage plastic recycling

topics.topic: Comprehensive Termly Revision & Civic Leadership Seminar
subtopics: Review of civic values, constitution, national symbols, and human rights
Interactive classroom youth leadership mock parliament
objectives: Complete JSS 1 Civic Education syllabus review

subtopics: Terminal examination and grading
objectives: Complete JSS 1 Civic Education certification
